sheet-4-1.description: Main part of sheet 4 of the May 1930 Sanborn atlas of Ridgewood, covering the western and central part of the borough of Hohokus (now Ho-Ho-Kus) at 100 ft to an inch. The Erie Railroad main line runs diagonally down the left side of the part, with Hohokus Brook crossing under it on a bridge; the Hohokus/Ridgewood village limits follow the brook and then the railroad. West of the tracks lies the Hohokus Bleachery, a large group of brick and frame buildings (dye house, dry houses, bleach house, wash and kier rooms, engine room, framing, folding and drawing out, calendars, packing and shipping, finished goods and supply warehouse) on the race of the brook, with a note on its watchman, heat, power and sprinkler system. Between the railroad and Franklin Turnpike are the Nagle Coal Co. yard with coal pockets and a motor oil warehouse, Stout Lane with a few dwellings, and large undeveloped blocks (385, 386). Hollywood Avenue crosses the top of the part; along Franklin Turnpike, Crescent Place, Ross Place, Carlton Avenue and Warren Place are detached frame dwellings, with long narrow lots on Knollwood Drive between the turnpike and the bluff above the brook. St. Bartholomew's Episcopal Church stands at Hollywood and Carlton Avenues. The New Jersey Rapid Transit Co.'s electric right of way crosses the upper right corner, and Richfield Plaza leads south over an iron bridge across the brook toward 1st Street. Sabin, north of Hollywood Avenue, is marked as an arbitrary (unbuilt) street. The lower left corner of the sheet is a separate inset at 150 ft to an inch (part 2).
notes: Franklin Turnpike north of Warren Avenue is now North Franklin Turnpike.
Sabin (marked arbitrary) corresponds to modern Hollywood Place.
Warren Place and Richfield Plaza are both now Warren Avenue.
Knollwood Drive and Stout Lane are not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Hohokus Bleachery on the brook west of the Erie main line.
Title cartouche reads Ridgewood N.J., May 1930; the sheet is the Hohokus section of the Ridgewood atlas.

Map, 100 ft. Printed sheet 4 of the Ridgewood 1930 atlas, Hohokus section (title cartouche reads Ridgewood N.J., Hohokus). Two parts. Part 1 (main): Hollywood Av, Franklin Turnpike (now North Franklin Turnpike), Crescent Pl, Sabin (paper street, now Hollywood Place), Carlton Av, Ross Pl, Warren Pl and Richfield Plaza (both now Warren Avenue), Knollwood Drive, 1st St, Erie main line, Hohokus Bleachery, Hohokus Brook. Part 2 (lower-left inset, 150 ft to an inch, separated by a heavy line): Hohokus Driving Park race track on Race Track Rd east of Edgewood Drive.

sheet-4-2.description: Inset in the lower left corner of sheet 4 of the May 1930 Sanborn atlas of Ridgewood, drawn at 150 ft to an inch and turned slightly against the main map, separated from it by a heavy border. It shows the Hohokus Driving Park on the north side of Race Track Road, east of Edgewood Drive, on the Hohokus/Ridgewood village limits, which run down the centre of Race Track Road. The oval race track fills most of the inset, with a grand stand and a judge's stand on its west side, an agricultural building, small frame sheds lettered C to F, a small electric pump and water tank, and a live stock pavilion at the east end near Race Track Road. A few dwellings stand along Race Track Road and on the east side of Edgewood Drive; Franklin Turnpike crosses the lower left corner. Most of the inset is open land (block 604). Numbers 137 and 149 south of Race Track Road refer to adjoining blocks. The inset is not joined to the main map of the sheet on the ground: it lies about 900 m to the east of the railroad shown there, at the south-east edge of the borough, adjoining the top right corner of sheet 8.
notes: Drawn at 150 ft to an inch, unlike the rest of the sheet (100 ft).
Placed from a hand-picked junction (Edgewood Drive / Race Track Road) and a point derived 1000 ft east along Race Track Road; low confidence.
The race track of the Hohokus Driving Park no longer exists; the area is now built over.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 of the May 1930 Sanborn atlas of Ridgewood, covering the centre of the borough of Hohokus (now Ho-Ho-Kus) at 100 ft to an inch, east of the area of sheet 4. Hollywood Avenue crosses the upper part from Gilbert Road and Sheridan Avenue to Lloyd Road; north of it are lots on Gilbert Road, Glendon Road, Fairlawn, Dixon and Jefferson. Warren Place (Boulevard) crosses the lower part, and Franklin Turnpike the lower left corner. Between them run Carlton Avenue, Sheridan Avenue, Sycamore Avenue, Elmwood Avenue, Lakewood Avenue and Lloyd Road, with Ross Place, Enos Place, Sherwood Road and Rich Court as cross streets. The abandoned North Jersey Rapid Transit Co. electric right of way crosses the sheet diagonally from Sheridan Avenue to Lakewood Avenue. Development is mostly detached frame dwellings with private garages on large lots, many blocks only partly built (blocks 392 to 404, 501 to 505). Institutions include the Hohokus Public School on Sheridan Avenue, the Hohokus Reformed Church at Warren Place and Sycamore Avenue, and the Hohokus Inn on Franklin Turnpike; a small concrete-block building of brick-faced stores stands at Sheridan Avenue and Franklin Turnpike. A brook runs south along Sheridan Avenue and east across the sheet, and Hohokus Brook enters at the lower right.
notes: Dixon, north of Hollywood Avenue, continues Elmwood Avenue; Jefferson continues Lakewood Avenue.
Fairlawn is now Fairlawn Street.
Warren Place (Boulevard) is now Warren Avenue.
North Jersey Rapid Transit Co. right of way (electric) marked abandoned.
Hohokus Public School, Hohokus Reformed Church and Hohokus Inn.
Sycamore Avenue / Warren Avenue and Sycamore Avenue / Franklin Turnpike were rejected by the fit (9 to 10 m), Hollywood Avenue / Lakewood Avenue and Hollywood Avenue / Lloyd Road likewise.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 of the May 1930 Sanborn atlas of Ridgewood, at 100 ft to an inch, straddling the Hohokus/Ridgewood village limit, which runs along 1st Street. The Erie Railroad main line runs down the middle of the sheet. West of it, in Ridgewood, is a residential district laid out on a grid: Hillcrest Road, Upper Boulevard (formerly Prospect), Summit Avenue and Adams (Cliff), crossed by Glenwood Road, Sherwood Road, Fairmount Road, California Street, Barrington Road (Madison), Phelps Road (Jefferson) and Wilson (Washington). Its blocks (23 to 39) carry detached frame dwellings, densest in the north, with many lots still empty in the south. East of the railroad the upper part lies in Hohokus: Brookside Avenue and 1st Street under Hohokus Brook, with dwellings, stores and the post office at Franklin Turnpike and North Maple Avenue. South of the limit, Cliff Street, 2nd Street, Pine and Undercliffe Court (Park Court) have small frame dwellings, and there is a group of stores on North Maple Avenue. The Hohokus passenger station and a freight house stand beside the tracks. Block numbers and the adjoining sheet numbers 4, 5, 6 and 8 are printed in the margins.
notes: Old names printed in parentheses: Upper Boulevard (Prospect), Barrington Road (Madison), Phelps Road (Jefferson), Wilson (Washington), Adams (Cliff), Undercliffe Court (Park Court).
Summit Avenue is now Summit Street, Wilson is Wilson Street, Pine is Pine Street, Undercliffe Court is Undercliff Court.

sheet-8-1.description: Main part of sheet 8 of the May 1930 Sanborn atlas of Ridgewood, at 100 ft to an inch, south and east of sheet 7 on both sides of the Hohokus/Ridgewood village limits, which follow 1st Street and Race Track Road across the upper part. Franklin Turnpike crosses the top from Sycamore Avenue to Edgewood Drive and Race Track Road, where it turns south-east. Along it are the Hohokus Borough Hall with the fire department, a garage with auto showroom, an auto repair shop, a filling station, a machine works and garage, and the brick office and shops of the North Jersey Rapid Transit Company; the company's abandoned electric right of way runs south through the sheet. North Maple Avenue (left edge) and Barrett Place have rows of frame dwellings and a second large garage. Hohokus Brook winds south through the middle of the sheet, dividing around an island and widening into the Mill Pond. The lower right corner is a newer subdivision at Van Buren (Madison Avenue), Northern Parkway (Lexington Avenue), Sterling Place, Thompson Place (3rd Street), Preston Place (2nd Street) and Allen Place (1st Street), and Conklin Place runs south from Franklin Turnpike. Much of the middle of the sheet is open land (blocks 135, 136, 138). The lower left corner is a separate inset (part 2).
notes: Barrett Place is now Barnett Place.
Conklin Place is now the north end of Northern Parkway.
Van Buren (Madison Avenue) is now Van Buren Street.

Franklin Turnpike has been realigned at Race Track Road: in 1930 it jogged along Race Track Road west of Edgewood Drive; the modern junction does not match the drawn one (about 13 m), so it was excluded.
Hohokus Borough Hall and fire department on Franklin Turnpike; North Jersey Rapid Transit Company office and shops (vacant part).
Only six control points; leave-one-out error about 6 m.

sheet-8-2.description: Inset in the lower left corner of sheet 8 of the May 1930 Sanborn atlas of Ridgewood, at 100 ft to an inch, framed by a heavy border. It continues the ground south of the main map between the match-line corners A and B, which are printed on both. It shows the Ridgewood Water Works, a small brick building with a coal bin and 80 ft iron chimney, on a lane with a 12 inch water pipe, in a large largely open block (138) north of East Glen Avenue (Harrison Avenue). George Street runs north from East Glen Avenue with a few frame dwellings and garages on both sides; the North Side Rapid Transit Co. right of way borders the inset on the east. Block 161 lies south of East Glen Avenue, and the number 9 refers to the adjoining sheet.
notes: Ridgewood Water Works.
East Glen Avenue was formerly Harrison Avenue.
Placed from East Glen Avenue / George Street and the two match-line corners A and B carried from the main part of the sheet.
